Audio recording is off. The mixer keeps running.
The encoder resolution may be smaller than the canvas. Free sizes are rounded to even numbers.
CBR is the default (used by YouTube); VBR follows image complexity; CQ keeps image quality steady.
CQ uses a quality value from 0 to 51 (lower is better). Bitrate is ignored while CQ is active; some device encoders reject this mode and fall back to VBR automatically.
Auto uses the High profile, then falls back to Baseline if the device rejects it.
Turn off to give recording its own bitrate.
The recording bitrate is used when recording without a live stream. When both run, the single encoder uses the bitrate of the session that started first.
Each AAC track has its own bitrate. Track 1 is the main mix.
Android MediaMuxer only supports MP4 for H.264/AAC.
Every track uses the same AAC encoder; extra tracks are written as separate tracks in the MP4.
Multitrack Video and WHIP Simulcast are not supported on Android yet; prepared for a later version.
The audio bitrate applies to the next capture session.
Audio devices and the mixer live in Settings → Audio; this page only configures the encoder and output tracks.
The encoder and bitrate are shared by recording and live; only one encoder runs.
Live sends track 1 (main mix). Tracks 2–6 are only for MP4 recordings.
Files are saved through MediaStore, so they appear in the gallery immediately without storage permission.
Long recordings are split into several files (_part2, _part3, …). Splits always start at a keyframe so each file plays on its own.
Keeps the last few seconds while recording. The Save replay button is in the record overlay panel.
Add RoutAir tiles to Quick Settings to start or stop recording without opening the app.
Username and password are sent on connect (server support varies).
Example: rtmp://a.rtmp.youtube.com/live2 with a separate stream key, or rtmps://server/application.
Try to reconnect when the connection drops (backoff 1–10 seconds).
Live uses the same encoder as recording, so record and live can run together. The stream key is stored locally on the device.
RoutAir combines several sources — screen, images, text, camera — into one scene, then records it to MP4 or streams it to YouTube.
Grant the following permissions once here. When you start recording later, only the screen capture dialog appears.
These two are opened through Android Settings, not a regular dialog.
RoutAir tests the phone capabilities, then picks the most suitable resolution, fps, and bitrate. You can rerun it anytime from Settings.
Press Record whenever you are ready. Advanced options live in the Settings tab.
Records audio for the recording and stream audio track.
Adds the camera as a scene source.
Pause and stop controls while the app is in the background.
Use a Bluetooth or TWS microphone.
Permissions are requested once here and can be changed anytime in Android Settings.
The floating record button over games or other apps.
Used only while the floating overlay is turned on.
Keeps recording from stopping when the screen is off or the app is in the background.
Some phone brands kill background apps; this permission prevents that.
Tests the encoder, resolution, and fps the phone can handle.
The result is applied to the canvas and recording right away.

Measures maximum H.264 and HEVC fps with synthetic frames, 5 seconds per codec. Stop recording or live first. These numbers are the encoder ceiling; recording fps is still limited by the fps setting and screen refresh rate.
Tests the phone capabilities, then picks the best resolution, fps, codec, and bitrate. For streaming, a 10-second upload test also runs when the stream key is filled in.
Prevents the screen and CPU from sleeping during the benchmark. Turn off to test behavior on screen timeout.
The in-video overlay shows fps, app CPU, RAM, render time (GPU load hint), thermal status, and remaining time. GPU percentage cannot be read by regular apps without system access.

Builds a heavy GL scene and CPU load similar to gaming, then records it using the resolution and fps template. No game or screen capture permission needed. Stop recording or live first. The fps shown is encoder fps, not game fps.
Physical hotkeys follow the connected keyboard. Quick Settings tiles are available for record and stop.
Save CPU when the screen is still
Drop to 30 fps when the screen does not change. Off = always full fps.
Drop to 30 fps when the device gets hot.
Both default to off: the encoder always runs at full fps.
Waiting for approval in the browser…
There is no stream key in this account yet. Open YouTube Studio > Live once to create one.
Google Play Services is not available on this device. Enter the stream key manually below.

Sign in to fill the server and stream key automatically and to enable chat. Without signing in, enter the stream key manually below (chat stays off). While the app is still in Testing status on Google Cloud, signing in again is required every 7 days.
this device has no hardware AV1 encoder
only a software AV1 encoder exists; not used because it is too slow
this device has no encoder for it
Size and fps limits reported by encoders are often narrower than reality. RoutAir tries the codec when a session starts; if it fails, it falls back to a supported codec and logs it.
Recording AV1 to MP4 requires Android 14 or newer; older versions cannot write the file.
HEVC/AV1 live uses Enhanced RTMP. YouTube supports it; other RTMP servers are checked automatically before streaming starts.
AV1 bitrate can be far lower than H.264 at the same quality (1080p60: 4–12 Mbps).
The current output resolution is the same as the canvas.

Vertical/Horizontal forces the display direction: the image is rotated 90° when needed and always loaded in full without cropping. Automatic follows the capture orientation. Adjust Position/Scale below.
